newsitem.title: USA: Toyota asks Arizona to terminate franchise rights.
newsitem.headline: Toyota asks Arizona to terminate franchise rights.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp. on Monday asked Arizona officials to terminate the franchise rights of a dealership that was purchased by Republic Industries Inc., the parent of the AutoNation superstore chain.

Toyota Motor Sales U.S.A. Inc., a unit of Toyota Motor Corp., said it would withdraw the request from the Arizona Department of Transportation if Republic backs away from its purchase of Tempe Toyota in Tempe, Ariz.
Toyota's action is the latest volley in a dispute between the Japanese carmaker and fast-growing Republic, a Fort Lauderdale, Fla.-based company controlled by billionaire Wayne Huizenga.

Toyota claims Republic and AutoNation want to buy as many as 59 Toyota dealerships in the United States, representing as much as 20 percent of Toyota's annual sales volume in the country. In addition to violating internal company policies about how many outlets a single owner can control, Toyota argues Republic's expansion plans could harm its brand identity and relationship with consumers.

In Arizona, Toyota says Republic has violated the requirements of state law governing multiple dealer ownerships. Monday's action was sparked by Republic's close on the sale of Tempe Toyota on June 23.
James Press, senior vice president at Toyota Motor Sales, said Republic "went behind our back" to close the sale, knowing that Toyota had not given it prior approval.

Press said business will continue as usual at the dealership until the Arizona officials rule, which could take 60 to 90 days. If the request is approved, Toyota would remove its vehicle inventory, signs and other equipment.
Republic spokesman James Donahue said Toyota's action was not unexpected. He said Toyota is now obligated to prove the franchise agreement should be terminated.

"We're a qualified buyer, Tempe is a willing seller and we don't believe that Toyota's artificial franchise agreements, which are largely self-serving, really is any substitute for the law of Arizona," he said.

Donahue also disputed Toyota's claims that Republic seeks to control 20 percent of Toyota's sales volume. If Republic buys all the dealerships it wants, it would account for "low single digits" of Toyota sales, he said.
In April, Toyota asked the Texas Motor Vehicle Board to halt the sale of a Houston dealership to Republic. The dealer withdrew from the sale before the board ruled.
